mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% in the month preceding the prediction horizon is associated with a short-term discounting effect that reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the preceding month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate surprises in late-cycle expansion
failure_condition: 20-day out-of-sample backtest shows no statistically significant negative returns during similar FEDFUNDS > 1.5% surprise events (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During 20 out-of-sample events matching the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS exceeding 10,000 jobs for two consecutive months indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 5 out-of-sample regime-matched windows, 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST and INDPRO show simultaneous monthly increases above their 12-month moving averages, it reflects robust industrial production and housing demand, which supports equity risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA and INDPRO > 12-month MA in the same month
regime_hint: Dual demand acceleration in recovery phase
failure_condition: During 10 such composite signals in out-of-sample, 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (decline > -5% month-on-month) combined with a sustained decline in GDPC1 (decline > -8% quarter-on-quarter) signals softening business activity and contracting demand, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During 8 out-of-sample events matching the trigger, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 5% for three consecutive months suggests a tightening labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During 12 such episodes in out-of-sample, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains persistently below 1% for four consecutive months, it signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers real rates, amplifying equity valuation expansion and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 7 out-of-sample windows with similar policy stance, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in RSAFS below 400 million dollars in two consecutive months, alongside a decline in HOUST below 1,000 units, indicates deteriorating demand conditions that can erode risk appetite and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 400M for 2 consecutive months AND HOUST < 1,000 for the same months
failure_condition: During 6 out-of-sample events with similar composites, 20-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.10).
